description: Change this mailbox's settings. Send only the fields to change. `displayName` is the sender name. `replyTo: null` goes back to the mailbox's own address, and `signatureText: null` is made from the HTML signature. `keepSentCopy` saves a copy of each email in the mailbox's Sent folder (never on Microsoft 365 or Outlook.com, which file their own copy, or on a send-only mailbox, which has no IMAP). `dailyCap` is how many emails it sends a day, warmup not counted, and `minGapSeconds` is the wait between two sends. `warmup` sets when warmup writes: `window` {opens, closes} as HH:MM on the workspace's clock, between 08:00 and 22:00 and at least 60 minutes apart, `days` (mon to sun), and `replyRatePct`, how often it answers instead of starting a new thread. `purpose` is `cold` (campaigns and new messages, the default) or `transactional` (only send_transactional_message, on a paid plan; it still receives mail and you can still reply). Changing `purpose`, either way, also needs the transactional permission (403 without it). A mailbox that campaigns send from, or with emails scheduled, can't become transactional: the 409 names up to 5 of those campaigns in `details.campaigns` ({id, name}). A send-only mailbox is always transactional (409).

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

purpose.description: What the mailbox sends. cold: campaigns and the messages people and agents write. transactional: only your app's transactional email (send_transactional_message), never outreach, and only on a paid plan. Either one still receives mail and warms up, unless it is a send-only mailbox. It can't become transactional while a campaign sends from it or an email from it is scheduled (409). A send-only mailbox is always transactional (409).
